input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# FIPS 140-3 crypto remediation for KServe serving images

## Description

Make every KServe component image (control plane and data plane) run correctly on
FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with no
non-validated crypto in the request path. This epic also delivers the KServe
portion of the FIPS regression enforcement and the inputs to the compliance
evidence package.

## Scope

- Audit all KServe images for non-validated cryptographic library usage and
  produce a per-image module inventory (libraries, versions, linkage, validation
  status).
- Remediate each flagged image to link only validated crypto modules (library
  swaps, rebuilds, base-image changes as needed) without changing functional
  behavior.
- Verify the remediated images on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters in both
  supported deployment modes (serverless and raw deployment).
- Author and verify the portion of the CI FIPS regression gating check that
  covers KServe builds: a gating check that fails any KServe build reintroducing
  non-validated crypto usage.
- Build the remediated images through the existing build pipeline (KServe is
  already onboarded) so that signed build attestations are produced and
  retrievable for the compliance evidence package.
- Hand off the module inventory, build attestations, and FIPS test results for
  aggregation into the compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A module inventory exists for every KServe image, enumerating each crypto
  library, its version, and its validation status.
- Scanning the built KServe images confirms no non-validated crypto modules are
  linked in the request path.
- Remediated images pass functional verification on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift
  cluster in both serverless and raw deployment modes.
- The CI FIPS regression check gates KServe builds and is verified to fail a
  deliberately non-compliant test build that reintroduces non-validated crypto
  usage.
- Remediated images build green in the existing build pipeline and their signed
  attestations are retrievable for the evidence package.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — KServe serving images run on FIPS-enabled clusters using
  validated crypto modules.
- **HLR-3 (P1)** — authors and verifies the CI FIPS regression gating check
  covering KServe builds. Bundled with the P0 remediation: the check shares the
  build surfaces, image inventories, and scan tooling of the remediation it
  enforces, so it is not separately schedulable — a standalone enforcement epic
  would re-audit the same builds.

## Risks / Notes

- The audit determines which specific images and libraries need work, but not
  the approach (audit → remediate → verify → enforce); the epic proceeds the
  same way regardless of the audit outcome.

Make the Platform Operator image run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift
clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with no non-validated crypto in

## Scope

- Audit the Platform Operator image for non-validated cryptographic library
  usage and produce a module inventory (libraries, versions, linkage, validation
  status).
- Remediate the image to link only validated crypto modules (library swaps,
  rebuilds, base-image changes as needed) without changing functional behavior.
- Verify the remediated image on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters (operator
  install/upgrade and reconciliation of managed serving components).
- Author and verify the portion of the CI FIPS regression gating check that
  covers Platform Operator builds: a gating check that fails any Platform
  Operator build reintroducing non-validated crypto usage.
- Build the remediated image through the existing build pipeline so that signed
  build attestations are produced and retrievable for the compliance evidence
  package.
- Hand off the module inventory, build attestations, and FIPS test results for
  aggregation into the compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A module inventory exists for the Platform Operator image, enumerating each
  crypto library, its version, and its validation status.
- Scanning the built image confirms no non-validated crypto modules are linked
  in the request path.
- The remediated image passes functional verification on a FIPS-enabled
  OpenShift cluster, including install/upgrade and reconciliation of managed
  serving components.
- The CI FIPS regression check gates Platform Operator builds and is verified to
  fail a deliberately non-compliant test build that reintroduces non-validated
  crypto usage.
- The remediated image builds green in the existing build pipeline and its
  signed attestations are retrievable for the evidence package.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — the Platform Operator image runs on FIPS-enabled clusters
  using validated crypto modules.
- **HLR-3 (P1)** — authors and verifies the CI FIPS regression gating check
  covering Platform Operator builds. Bundled with the P0 remediation: the check
  shares the build surfaces and scan tooling of the remediation it enforces, so
  it is not separately schedulable — a standalone enforcement epic would
  re-audit the same builds.

  regardless of the audit outcome.

# FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and certification submission

## Description

Assemble the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model serving stack
(module inventory, build attestations, test results) and submit it through the
security review board to the external accredited certification laboratory.

## Scope

- Aggregate the per-image crypto module inventories, signed build attestations,
  and FIPS test results produced by the KServe and Platform Operator
  remediation work.
- Assemble the evidence package in the format required by the security review
  board and the external certification laboratory.
- Drive the package through the mandatory security review board sign-off at the
  defined milestones and submit it to the external accredited laboratory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains the complete module inventory, build
  attestations, and FIPS test results for every serving-stack image in scope,
  and is internally consistent: every image in the inventory is covered by
  attestations and test results.
- The evidence package includes the signed attestations produced by the
  components' build pipelines.
- The evidence package is submitted through the security review board to the
  external accredited certification laboratory.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)** — compliance evidence package (module inventory, build
  attestations, test results) assembled and submitted through the security
  review board to the external certification lab.

## Risks / Notes

- Certification lab turnaround is historically six to nine months and the
  security review board cadence is fixed; both are externally controlled and
  cannot be compressed by engineering effort. They dominate the schedule and are
  recorded here as risks, not as acceptance criteria.
- The certification outcome and its timing rest with the external laboratory;
  engineering controls the package assembly and submission only.

# FIPS support posture documentation

## Description

Document the FIPS support posture of the model serving stack and the cluster
prerequisites for running it on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters, reflecting the
delivered remediation and certification state.

## Scope

Content outline:
- FIPS support posture of the model serving stack: what is supported, the
  certification status, and how the external certification timeline affects it.
- Cluster prerequisites: FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters and validated
  cryptographic modules.
- Deployment-mode guidance where the posture differs between serverless and raw
  deployment modes.
- Any user-facing behavior changes introduced by the crypto remediation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the FIPS support posture of the model serving
  stack and the cluster prerequisites for running it on FIPS-enabled clusters.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented remediation and
  evidence results by the implementing engineers.
- All user-facing behavior changes introduced by the crypto remediation are
  documented.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)** — documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster
  prerequisites.

Notes on assignments:

  (`.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/kserve.md`: owning team
  RHOAI Serving, midstream `opendatahub-io/kserve`, Konflux-onboarded).
- E003 spans both affected components (it aggregates evidence from the KServe and

  canonical component, KServe, because the strategy targets the model serving
  stack of which KServe is the primary component.
- E004 is assigned the canonical `Documentation` component (Red Hat docs content
  process → `docs-authoring`).
- Team assignments for E002 and E004 are inferred — the strategy has no Impacted
  Teams table (see Health Warnings).

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9013-E001 KServe remediation] --> E003[RHAISTRAT-9013-E003 evidence package]
    E002[RHAISTRAT-9013-E002 Platform Operator remediation] --> E003
    E001 --> E004[RHAISTRAT-9013-E004 docs]
    E002 --> E004
    E003 --> E004
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E003 | Rule 12/13 (artifact producer → consumer) | The evidence package documents the remediated KServe images, their module inventory, and FIPS test results; it cannot be assembled before that work exists. Build attestations, however, are consumed as content: expressed as an acceptance criterion on E003, never as an edge to any build-pipeline work. |
| E002 → E003 | Rule 12/13 (artifact producer → consumer) | Same: evidence for the Platform Operator image depends on its remediation results. |
| E001 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | docs-authoring epic blocked by every Implementation epic in the strategy. |
| E002 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Same. |
| E003 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Same. |
| (no edge) E001 ∥ E002 | Rule 14 (different components/repos) | Remediation work in different components with no shared artifacts runs in parallel. |
| (no edge) build pipelines → E003 | Rule 13 / Rule 10 | KServe is already Konflux-onboarded per architecture context, so no onboarding epics are generated; the signed attestations the evidence package needs are a configuration/content reference — an AC on E003, not a DAG dependency. |
| (no epic) CI FIPS regression gate | Shared-surface enforcement rule | HLR-3's gating check spans the exact builds and images the remediation epics modify — it is divided per surface into E001 and E002 (each authors and verifies the portion covering its own builds), not carved into a standalone work-type epic. |

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Coverage |
|-----|----------|---------|----------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | E001, E002 | E001 covers all KServe images; E002 covers the Platform Operator image. Together they cover "all serving-stack images" across the strategy's affected components. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | E003 | Evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | E001, E002 (bundled) — the CI gating check shares the build surfaces, image inventories, and scan tooling of the P0 remediation it enforces; per the shared-surface enforcement rule it is divided per surface into the epic that owns each surface, and a standalone CI epic would re-audit the same builds twice. Not separately schedulable. | Each remediation epic authors and verifies the portion of the FIPS regression gating check covering its own component's builds. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | E004 | Documentation of FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites; docs-authoring priority derived from strategy priority Critical → P0 per the docs-authoring priority exception. |

All four HLRs are covered; none orphaned.

## Health Warnings

1. **Missing strategy sections.** The strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
   Dependencies table, no Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then) section, and no
   Non-Functional Requirements; the Affected Components section is a bare list
   without per-component change descriptions or owner teams. Decomposition
   proceeded from the HLRs and the component list; team assignments for E002
   (Platform Operator) and E004 (Documentation) are inferred and need human
   verification.
2. **Platform Operator has no architecture-context file.**
   `.context/architecture-context/` contains only `kserve.md`. The Platform
   Operator's repos, surfaces, and owning team could not be corroborated. It is
   treated as an existing component being remediated — it appears in the canonical
   RHAI component list (`.context/rhai-components.txt`) and the strategy presumes
   it exists ("affected component"), so no onboarding chain was generated — but
   this premise is unverified; flag for human review. AI signal
   `architecture_claims` is scored 0 for E002.
3. **Scope ambiguity — "serving data plane".** The problem statement says "KServe
   components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries",
   but Affected Components lists only KServe and Platform Operator. Per the KServe
   architecture context, the serving data plane executes on Serving Runtimes
   (vLLM, OpenVINO, Caikit), which are NOT listed as affected, and the
   out-of-scope list does not mention them. If the data-plane runtime images are
   in scope, an additional Serving Runtimes remediation epic is required. The
   decomposition follows the Affected Components list (the authoritative input to
   epic generation); human verification needed before execution.
4. **External schedule gates are risks, not acceptance criteria.** Certification
   lab turnaround (historically six to nine months) and security review board
   cadence are externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering
   effort. They are recorded as Risks/Notes on the evidence epic; the AC sits at
   the engineering completion point we control (package assembled and submitted).
5. **Priority notes (not inversions).** HLR-3 (P1) is bundled into the P0
   remediation epics (see traceability row for rationale), and HLR-4 (P2) maps to
   a P0 docs epic because the docs-authoring priority exception derives it from
   the strategy's Critical priority. Both are rule-driven.

## Tiered Delivery

The external certification dependency has uncertain timing, and the strategy can
deliver partial value without it:

- **Tier 1 (independent value):** E001 and E002. FIPS-capable serving-stack
  images plus CI regression enforcement deliver user-facing value (the serving
  stack runs correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters) without certification.
- **Tier 2 (dependency-gated):** E003 (evidence package and submission — gated on
  the Tier 1 remediation results and, externally, on review-board and lab
  timing) and E004 (blocked by all Implementation epics per the docs-last rule).

## Component Mapping Notes

- All epic `component` values are verbatim from `.context/rhai-components.txt`:
  `KServe` (E001, E003), `Platform Operator` (E002), `Documentation` (E004).
- E003 spans KServe and Platform Operator; assigned `KServe` as the single most
  relevant canonical name (noted above).

## Investigation Epic Decision

No Investigation epics were generated. The strategy declares "None on scope" for
open questions; the remaining unknown — exactly which images link which
non-validated crypto libraries — does not change which epics exist (both affected
components are declared affected regardless) or their approach (audit →
remediate → verify → enforce). Per the unclear-passage distinction this is an
implementation detail resolved when each remediation epic starts, captured as the
module-inventory acceptance criterion on E001 and E002. Lab scheduling and
review-board cadence are external schedule constraints (Health Warning 4), not
technical unknowns.
